questions.question: how much rest does a US airline have to give a flight attendant between duty days

sources.passage: A flight attendant scheduled to a duty period of 14 hours or less as provided under paragraph (b)(1) of this section must be given a scheduled rest period of at least 10 consecutive hours.

key.item: Rest after a duty period of 14 hours or less

key.answer: may not be reduced to less than 10 consecutive hours

questions.commonly_confused: 9 consecutive hours, reducible to 8, is the rule as it stood before 2022.

questions.question: At what alcohol concentration is a US commercial motor vehicle driver barred from safety-sensitive duty under the federal drug and alcohol testing rules?

sources.passage: No driver shall report for duty or remain on duty requiring the performance of safety-sensitive functions while having an alcohol concentration of 0.04 or greater.

questions.commonly_confused: 0.08 is the usual state limit for private drivers; 0.02 triggers a separate 24-hour removal.

questions.question: how heavy can a drone be and still count as a small drone under the FAA rules

sources.passage: Small unmanned aircraft means an unmanned aircraft weighing less than 55 pounds on takeoff, including everything that is on board or otherwise attached to the aircraft.

key.answer: everything on board or otherwise attached

questions.commonly_confused: It is less than 55 pounds, not 55 or less; 0.55 pounds is the registration threshold, a different rule.

difficulty: a sum the sources do not state
questions.question: How much paid annual leave does a worker in Great Britain get by statute, in weeks, and what is the cap in days?

sources.passage: a worker is entitled to four weeks' annual leave in each leave year.
The aggregate entitlement provided for in paragraph (2) and regulation 13(1) is subject to a maximum of 28 days.

questions.commonly_confused: Four weeks alone is the EU-derived minimum; 5.6 is the two regulations together.

questions.question: What are the basic VFR weather minimums in Class E airspace below 10,000 feet MSL: flight visibility and distance from clouds?

sources.passage: Less than 10,000 feet MSL 3 statute miles 500 feet below. 1,000 feet above. 2,000 feet horizontal.

key.answer: 500 feet below, 1,000 feet above, 2,000 feet horizontal

questions.commonly_confused: 5 statute miles and 1,000/1,000/1 mile is the row for at or above 10,000 feet MSL.

questions.question: In the original DNS specification, what are the size limits on a label and on a full domain name, in octets?

sources.passage: labels 63 octets or less names 255 octets or less

questions.commonly_confused: 253 is the longest name as usually written in text, not the limit the specification states.

difficulty: an older limit is still widely quoted
questions.question: What are OSHA's permissible exposure limit and action level for respirable crystalline silica in general industry?

sources.passage: The employer shall ensure that no employee is exposed to an airborne concentration of respirable crystalline silica in excess of 50 µg/m3, calculated as an 8-hour TWA.

questions.commonly_confused: The older limit was a formula in Table Z-3, about 100 µg/m3 for pure quartz.

questions.question: What is the US federal maximum contaminant level for PFOA in drinking water? Give it as the rule lists it and in nanograms per litre.
questions.commonly_confused: 70 parts per trillion was the 2016 health advisory, not a limit; 10 ng/L is the figure for other PFAS.

questions.commonly_confused: 9.3 is the same record's version 2.0 score.

questions.question: In the IANA HTTP status code registry, what is the name of status code 425 and which RFC is its reference?
questions.commonly_confused: 425 was once listed as Unordered Collection in a WebDAV draft.

questions.question: In Robert's Rules of Order as first published in 1876, the pocket manual that Project Gutenberg carries, what vote does the manual require to adopt a motion for the Previous Question?

sources.passage: a two-thirds vote be required, as in this Manual [§ 39], for sustaining an objection to the introduction of a question, or for adopting a motion for the Previous Question

questions.commonly_confused: A bare majority is the rule of the US House of Representatives, which the manual sets aside for ordinary societies.

questions.question: From Texas Instruments' LM317 datasheet: what is the absolute maximum input-output voltage differential, and what is the typical reference voltage?
questions.commonly_confused: 37 V is the top of the adjustable output range, not the differential rating.

questions.question: In the SI Brochure, 9th edition, what value is fixed for the luminous efficacy Kcd, and for monochromatic radiation of what frequency?

sources.passage: the luminous efficacy of monochromatic radiation of frequency 540 × 1012 Hz, Kcd, is 683 lm/W

questions.commonly_confused: 555 nm is the wavelength in air usually quoted; the definition is by frequency.

difficulty: the rule does not answer the question
a near answer is in the same section
questions.question: Under 14 CFR § 91.151, what fuel reserve must a glider carry to begin a flight under VFR conditions?

sources.passage: No person may begin a flight in a rotorcraft under VFR conditions unless (considering wind and forecast weather conditions) there is enough fuel to fly to the first point of intended landing and, assuming normal cruising speed, to fly after that for at least 20 minutes.

key.answer: none is stated: the section sets reserves for airplanes and for rotorcraft only

questions.commonly_confused: 30 or 45 minutes is the airplane rule and 20 minutes the rotorcraft rule; giving either for a glider is wrong.

difficulty: a worked case, not a definition
questions.question: A liquid has a flash point of 65 °C and meets the definition of no other hazard class. For transport under the US hazardous materials regulations, is it a Class 3 flammable liquid, and if not, what is it?

sources.passage: a combustible liquid means any liquid that does not meet the definition of any other hazard class specified in this subchapter and has a flash point above 60 °C (140 °F) and below 93 °C (200 °F).

key.answer: no: its flash point is above 60 °C (140 °F)
a combustible liquid: flash point above 60 °C (140 °F) and below 93 °C (200 °F)

questions.commonly_confused: Calling it flammable because 65 °C is 'close to' 60 °C; the definition is a hard line.

difficulty: three limits are easily mixed up
questions.question: how long can a trucker drive before they have to take a break

sources.passage: driving is not permitted if more than 8 hours of driving time have passed without at least a consecutive 30-minute interruption in driving status.

key.answer: at least a consecutive 30-minute interruption in driving status

questions.commonly_confused: 11 hours is the total driving limit and 14 hours the on-duty window; neither is the break rule.

difficulty: two limits on different time bases
questions.question: What dose limits does the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission set for individual members of the public from a licensee's operations: per year, and in any one hour in an unrestricted area?

sources.passage: The total effective dose equivalent to individual members of the public from the licensed operation does not exceed 0.1 rem (1 mSv) in a year

questions.commonly_confused: 5 rems is the occupational limit for workers, fifty times higher.
